newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Second bomb in two months near Budapest synagogue.
newsitem.headline: Second bomb in two months near Budapest synagogue.

text.p: A bomb exploded on Wednesday in a dustbin near Hungary's main synagogue in the latest in a series of explosions in the capital.
The blast, near Budapest's Dohanyi Utca Synagogue, Europe's largest, hurled bits of the dustbin over an area of 100 metres (yards).
A similar attack took place in October at the same spot.
"I don't know anything but it seems to me that no-one was hurt," a policeman told Reuters minutes after the explosion, which happened at 7.10 p.m.
The explosion was heard several blocks away in the centre of Hungary's commercial district.
Since September, Budapest has been shaken by 11 bombings and five shootings, apparently in a war between organised gangs. One man has been killed and two have been badly injured.
The Hungarian government sacked the chiefs of the national and Budapest police on Friday for failing to halt gangland bombings and shootings in the capital.
A homemade bomb exploded near the synagogue in October scattering debris up to 20 metres but causing no injuries.
Other bombings have been targeted at businesses and nightclubs in the capital.
